official_sources.title: NumPy argmax first-occurrence semantics
official_sources.finding: argmax returns only the first occurrence when the maximum value appears multiple times, so it cannot by itself preserve the full extrema tie-set.

official_sources.title: NumPy argmin first-occurrence semantics
official_sources.finding: argmin returns only the first occurrence when the minimum value appears multiple times, so terminal extrema provenance must enumerate all equal minima separately.

official_sources.title: NumPy flattened argmax indexing
official_sources.finding: With axis=None, argmax returns an index into the flattened array; flattening order therefore cannot be left implicit when replaying a chosen cell.

official_sources.title: NumPy flattened argmin indexing
official_sources.finding: With axis=None, argmin returns an index into the flattened array and can be converted back with unravel_index.

official_sources.title: NumPy nonzero row-major ordering
official_sources.finding: nonzero returns indices in row-major C-style order, providing a documented deterministic enumeration order for a boolean tie mask.

official_sources.title: NumPy argwhere grouped coordinates
official_sources.finding: argwhere groups coordinates by element into an (N, ndim) array, useful for explicit row/column tie-set materialization.

official_sources.title: NumPy flatnonzero flattened candidates
official_sources.finding: flatnonzero returns nonzero indices in the flattened input, giving a separate flattened tie-mask replay path.

official_sources.title: NumPy unravel_index coordinate recovery
official_sources.finding: unravel_index converts flat indices back to coordinate tuples and accepts an explicit order parameter, so row/column recovery can be versioned.

official_sources.title: NumPy ravel_multi_index coordinate encoding
official_sources.finding: ravel_multi_index converts coordinate arrays to flat indices and exposes order and out-of-bounds modes; terminal replay must use raise semantics rather than wrap or clip.

official_sources.title: NumPy lexsort stable multi-key ordering
official_sources.finding: lexsort performs an indirect stable multi-key sort; the last key is primary and earlier keys break ties in defined sequence.

official_sources.title: NumPy stable argsort
official_sources.finding: argsort supports stable=True, preserving relative order of equal values; unstable default behavior must not define terminal tie ordering.

official_sources.title: NumPy stable sort
official_sources.finding: sort supports stable=True and documents that equal items preserve relative order only under a stable sort.

official_sources.title: NumPy structured-key tie breaking
official_sources.finding: Structured-array sort can use explicit field order to break ties, supporting value,row,column deterministic ordering.

official_sources.title: NumPy argsort structured-key order
official_sources.finding: argsort accepts explicit field order for structured arrays, enabling indirect deterministic ordering of extrema records.

official_sources.title: NumPy array_equal exact replay
official_sources.finding: array_equal tests whether arrays have the same shape and elements, making it appropriate for exact tie-set coordinate replay rather than tolerance-based acceptance.

official_sources.title: NumPy equal elementwise equality
official_sources.finding: equal performs element-wise equality and can build exact masks for cells whose decoded value equals the terminal minimum or maximum.

official_sources.title: NumPy allclose tolerance caveat
official_sources.finding: allclose is tolerance-based and asymmetric in its reference argument; default tolerances are not suitable as an implicit definition of exact extrema ties.

official_sources.title: NumPy count_nonzero tie count
official_sources.finding: count_nonzero counts true/nonzero elements and can independently verify the cardinality of a boolean extrema tie mask.

official_sources.title: NumPy nanargmin semantics
official_sources.finding: nanargmin ignores NaNs but remains a single-index selector; an all-NaN or invalid candidate region must not be converted into a fabricated extrema cell.

official_sources.title: NumPy nanargmax semantics
official_sources.finding: nanargmax ignores NaNs but remains a single-index selector; terminal logic still needs the complete valid equal-maximum set.

official_sources.title: NumPy NaN distinct from infinity
official_sources.finding: NumPy documents NaN as distinct from infinity under IEEE-754, so invalid-value filtering must occur before extrema tie selection.

official_sources.title: NumPy sorting/searching routine separation
official_sources.finding: NumPy exposes separate extrema-index, nonzero, stable sorting and counting operations; deterministic tie-set construction can therefore be independently replayed from primitive steps.

official_sources.title: GDAL actual edge-block size
official_sources.finding: GetActualBlockSize returns the true valid pixel dimensions for partial edge blocks, preventing padded block cells from entering extrema.

official_sources.title: GDAL natural block size
official_sources.finding: GetBlockSize exposes the band's natural block dimensions, which can vary independently of raster dimensions and must not alter logical row/column identity.

official_sources.title: GDAL ReadBlock block addressing
official_sources.finding: ReadBlock addresses blocks by zero-based block offsets; block traversal order is an implementation detail and must not define tie winner semantics.

official_sources.title: GDAL pixel-info column/line replay
official_sources.finding: gdal raster pixel-info reports input coordinates converted to column/line and pixel values, providing independent QA for each extrema cell.

official_sources.title: GDAL pixel-info unscaled value
official_sources.finding: pixel-info reports pixel values including unscaled values, allowing extrema ledger checks against the physical decode path.

official_sources.title: GDAL VRT contributing-source pixel QA
official_sources.finding: For VRT inputs pixel-info can report contributing source files, enabling tie cells to retain source provenance rather than only a numeric value.

official_sources.title: GDAL as-features one feature per pixel
official_sources.finding: gdal raster as-features creates one feature per pixel instead of combining adjacent equal values, providing an independent pixel-wise extrema enumeration path.

official_sources.title: GDAL as-features skip nodata path
official_sources.finding: The as-features workflow supports skipping nodata pixels, reinforcing that invalid cells must be excluded before extrema membership.

official_sources.title: GDAL raster compare golden semantics
official_sources.finding: gdal raster compare treats the reference dataset as the exact/golden dataset and reports differences, supporting golden replay of extracted extrema windows.

official_sources.title: GDAL raster compare geotransform metadata
official_sources.finding: Raster compare can check binary content, CRS, geotransform, overviews and metadata, so equal extrema numbers alone are insufficient for terminal raster identity.

official_sources.title: GDAL gdalcompare pixel-difference reporting
official_sources.finding: gdalcompare reports pixel differences and maximum pixel difference against a golden image, supporting independent exact-window replay.

official_sources.title: GDAL raster info band metadata
official_sources.finding: gdal raster info reports band datatype, block size, description, nodata, unit and optional checksum, allowing extrema records to bind to exact band identity.

official_sources.title: GDAL approximate stats warning
official_sources.finding: --approx-stats may use overviews or only a subset of tiles, so approximate min/max metadata cannot replace exact parcel extrema.

official_sources.title: GDAL checksum QA
official_sources.finding: gdal raster info can force per-band checksum computation, providing an additional immutable replay signal for the source band.

official_sources.title: GDAL raster command separation
official_sources.finding: GDAL separates pixel-info, compare, as-features, overview and other operations, enabling independent terminal cross-checks without relying on one code path.

official_sources.title: NumPy where conditional index bridge
official_sources.finding: When only a condition is supplied, where is a shorthand for nonzero; terminal tie enumeration should therefore prefer explicit nonzero semantics and preserve the boolean tie mask.
